title: Orbit Cascade
premise: A neon sci-fi physics merge game where the player drops glowing drone-like spheres into a vertical orbital chamber and combines matching units into larger forms before the stack reaches the danger line.
interaction_model: Mouse or touch controls the horizontal drop position; click or tap releases the queued sphere into a gravity-driven bounded playfield.
objective: Survive as long as possible and earn a high score by repeatedly merging identical spheres into larger orbit-class units while preventing the pile from stabilizing near the top boundary.
progression: The run starts with only small spawn types, then naturally escalates as merges create larger, space-consuming spheres that make the chamber harder to manage until eventual overflow causes game over.
theme: Cosmic neon arcade with abstract orbital drones and glowing energy cores.
mood: Sleek, vibrant, tense, and satisfying, mixing chill sci-fi ambience with rising stack-management pressure.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy casual browser arcade games, Suika-style merge puzzles, score-chasing experiences, and touch-friendly one-screen physics games.
confidence_notes: High confidence on the core gameplay loop, controls, scoring, and fail condition because they are directly implemented in code. Moderate confidence on thematic wording because the sphere data still resembles a fruit-merge template internally even though the UI and presentation clearly reframe it as orbit drones.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished one-screen browser game called 'Orbit Cascade' that plays like a futuristic Suika-style physics merge puzzle. Present a tall bounded chamber in the center of the screen with neon cyan, violet, and pink accents, a starry sci-fi backdrop, a start screen, a HUD showing score and the next piece, and a game-over overlay with final score and retry. The player should move a horizontal drop position with mouse or touch and click or tap to release a glowing spherical drone from the top into the chamber. Gravity pulls spheres downward, they bounce softly off walls and floor, collide physically with each other, and two spheres of the same tier should merge into the next larger tier at their midpoint, awarding score and creating a satisfying pop. Only the first few small tiers should spawn naturally, so progression emerges through merges into larger and larger units. Show a ghost preview at the drop point and a separate next-piece preview in the HUD. Add ambient background particles, glossy glow shading on spheres, subtle feedback animations, looping background music, and sound effects for start, drop, collision, merge, and failure. The loss condition should happen when the stack reaches a top danger line and a sphere settles there, ending the run. The overall feel should be accessible, mobile-friendly, replayable, and focused on careful placement, chain merges, space management, and score chasing.
